name: TCF Canada
notes: Listening and reading are scored from 0 to 699; writing and speaking from 0 to 20.
Speaking per-task timings below are commonly reported; check the official candidate handbook before relying on them.

co.name: Compréhension orale
co.format: Multiple choice on recorded documents of increasing difficulty.
strategy: Questions get harder as you go: bank easy points early.
Read the options before the audio and predict the topic.
Listen for paraphrase: the right option rarely repeats the exact words.

ce.name: Compréhension écrite
ce.format: Multiple choice on documents of increasing difficulty.
strategy: Difficulty rises through the test: keep time for the long texts at the end.
Identify the document type and purpose first.
Eliminate options that are true but do not answer the question.

ee.name: Expression écrite

sections.title: Article / compte rendu
sections.en: An article, letter or report on an experience

sections.title: Comparer deux points de vue
sections.en: Present two opposing views, then take a position

strategy: Respect the word ranges: too short or too long costs points.
Task 3: summarize BOTH documents neutrally first, then give your own reasoned opinion.
Vary sentence structures and connectors; reread for agreement.

eo.name: Expression orale

sections.title: Exercice en interaction
sections.en: Interaction: ask the examiner questions to get information (5.5 min including 2 min preparation, so about 3.5 min speaking)

sections.title: Expression d’un point de vue
sections.en: Give and justify your opinion on a topic

strategy: Task 1: talk about yourself in detail — family, work, interests, plans.
Task 2: ask many varied questions (who, what, when, how much…) and react to answers.
Task 3: give a clear opinion, two or three arguments, and an example from your life.
